fragments.title: The Preparation
fragments.content: The house was spotless, the food was ready, the guests would arrive soon. Julia would worry about the details, but I had everything under control. This party was more than just a gathering - it was a thread connecting us to those who had gone before.

sensoryDetails.visual: Tables set with fine china and crystal
sensoryDetails.auditory: The clink of glasses being polished
sensoryDetails.tactile: The smooth linen tablecloth beneath my fingers

fragments.title: The Old Song
fragments.content: They asked me to sing tonight, and I did. My voice was stronger than it had been in years. There is a joy in giving voice to memories, in letting the old songs live again through me. The years fall away when I sing.

sensoryDetails.visual: The sheet music, yellow with age
sensoryDetails.auditory: My own voice, trembling but true
sensoryDetails.tactile: The worn leather cover of the songbook

fragments.title: The Hatred of the South
fragments.content: Molly Ivors accused me of being a West Briton because I write for The Daily Express. She wanted me to visit the Aran Isles with her, to reconnect with my Irish heritage. But I couldn't - I felt nothing for Ireland, only contempt for its provinciality. My soul belonged elsewhere, to Europe, to culture, to ideas.

sensoryDetails.visual: Molly's freckled face, flushed with anger

fragments.title: The Speech
fragments.content: I stood before the guests, my voice trembling slightly as I began my speech. I spoke of the past, of old friends and cherished traditions. But beneath the words, I felt a strange emptiness, as if I were performing rather than speaking from the heart. I quoted Browning - 'One feels that one is listening to a thought-tormented music' - and saw Miss Ivors nod approvingly.

sensoryDetails.visual: The soft glow of gas lamps on polished silver
sensoryDetails.auditory: The murmur of voices, the rustle of silk dresses
sensoryDetails.tactile: The coldness of the champagne flute in my hand

fragments.title: The Lass of Aughrim
fragments.content: The song drifted across the room, and suddenly I was back in Galway, standing in the rain, waiting for Michael. I could feel the cold, hear his voice calling my name. The years fell away, and for a moment, he was there again - young, vibrant, full of love. My eyes filled with tears I could not control.

sensoryDetails.visual: Michael's face, pale in the moonlight
sensoryDetails.auditory: His voice, clear and strong, singing my song
sensoryDetails.tactile: The cold rain soaking through my shawl

context.situation: Hearing Bartell D'Arcy sing 'The Lass of Aughrim'

fragments.title: Gretta's Distraction
fragments.content: I noticed Gretta standing by the window, listening to the song. There was a look on her face I had never seen before - a look of such deep longing that it frightened me. I called her name, but she did not hear. In that moment, I realized I did not know the woman I had married.

sensoryDetails.visual: Gretta's silhouette against the dark window
sensoryDetails.auditory: The faint strains of 'The Lass of Aughrim'
sensoryDetails.tactile: The chill of realization creeping over me

fragments.title: The Promise
fragments.content: I waited for her in the snow, my coat thin against the winter cold. I had to see her, to tell her how much I loved her. Even as the frost bit into my bones, I could not leave. She was worth every shiver, every breath. I would show her what love truly meant.

sensoryDetails.visual: The white blanket of snow covering everything
sensoryDetails.auditory: The wind howling through the empty streets
sensoryDetails.tactile: The freezing cold seeping into my very soul

context.place: Outside Gretta's grandmother's house in Galway
context.situation: Waiting for Gretta before she leaves for Dublin

fragments.title: The Rainy Night
fragments.content: I heard gravel against my window and ran downstairs. There he was, standing in the rain, so pale, so thin. I begged him to go home, but he wouldn't listen. He said he didn't want to live without me. I should have been kinder. I should have told him I loved him, even though I was leaving.

sensoryDetails.visual: His dark eyes, gleaming with unshed tears
sensoryDetails.auditory: The rain drumming on the roof
sensoryDetails.tactile: His cold, wet hands in mine

fragments.title: The News
fragments.content: A week after I arrived in Dublin, the letter came. Pneumonia, they said. He had caught his death waiting for me in the rain. I never saw him again. I never said goodbye. That song - it still breaks my heart every time I hear it.

sensoryDetails.visual: The black-bordered letter in my hands
sensoryDetails.auditory: My own sobbing echoing in the empty room
sensoryDetails.tactile: The paper, crumpled from my grip

context.time: One week after arriving in Dublin

fragments.title: The Journey Home
fragments.content: In the cab, I felt so alive, so certain of my love for Gretta. I imagined running after her, catching her, whispering foolish things in her ear. But now I see it was all illusion - a romance I invented in my own mind. The truth was far different.

sensoryDetails.visual: The snow-covered streets outside the cab window
sensoryDetails.auditory: The horse's hooves on the cobblestones
sensoryDetails.tactile: The warmth of her arm against mine

context.place: Cab on the way to the hotel

fragments.title: The Last Thought
fragments.content: As the darkness closed in, I thought only of her - her smile, her laugh, the way she said my name. I did not regret what I had done. Love is not measured in years, but in moments. And in that moment, I was truly alive. She would remember me. That was enough.

sensoryDetails.visual: A flash of Gretta's face in the darkness
sensoryDetails.tactile: The gentle warmth of memory replacing the cold

fragments.title: The Confession
fragments.content: She told me about Michael - how he died for her, how he waited in the rain. I wanted to be angry, but I couldn't. I had never loved like that, never been loved like that. All my talk of passion was hollow. I was a ridiculous figure, playing at love.

sensoryDetails.visual: Her face, wet with tears, averted from mine
sensoryDetails.auditory: The sound of her sobs muffled against the quilt
sensoryDetails.tactile: Her hand, cold and unresponsive in mine

fragments.title: The Truth
fragments.content: I didn't mean to tell him, but the song had broken something open in me. All these years, Michael lived in my heart, a secret I could never share. Gabriel deserved to know, even if it hurt him. Perhaps now we could begin again, honestly.

sensoryDetails.visual: Gabriel's face, frozen in the lamplight
sensoryDetails.auditory: My own voice, strange and distant
sensoryDetails.tactile: The quilt rough against my cheek

fragments.title: The Epiphany
fragments.content: I watched her sleep, and for the first time, I truly saw her - not as my wife, not as my possession, but as a woman with a past, with losses I could never understand. The snow was falling on all of Ireland, on the living and the dead. I was neither, only a shadow passing between worlds.

sensoryDetails.visual: Snowflakes falling silently in the moonlight
sensoryDetails.tactile: The cold glass against my forehead

context.situation: Watching Gretta sleep, understanding at last

fragments.title: Generous Tears
fragments.content: I had never felt like that myself towards any woman, but I knew that such a feeling must be love. Michael Furey had braved death for Gretta, and she had carried that image in her heart for all these years. I could not compete with a dead man. Perhaps I never could.

sensoryDetails.visual: The form of Michael, standing under a dripping tree
sensoryDetails.auditory: The snow falling faintly, like the descent of their last end

context.situation: Weeping for what he never had
